environment: This is Node.js ESM code, so it runs in strict mode, with no external packages. Predict before running it; we can run it after your answer.

cases.surface: object method called directly and then through a detached reference
cases.question: Predict the three lines of output. What decides this in each of the two calls?

criteria.description: Explains that this comes from the call form: counter.increment() sets counter as the receiver, while a plain call of the detached function leaves this undefined in strict mode, so reading this.count throws.

wrongModels.claim: A method keeps the object it was defined on as this wherever it is called from.
A plain call uses the global object as this, so the count becomes NaN on globalThis.

cases.surface: regular function versus arrow function passed to map inside a method
cases.question: Predict the two lines of output. Why do the two callbacks see different values of this?

criteria.description: Explains that map calls the regular callback without a receiver, so its own this is undefined, while the arrow callback has no own this and uses the method's this, which is team.

wrongModels.claim: A nested function inherits this from the method that contains it.
Arrow functions have no this at all, so this.name is undefined inside them.

cases.surface: class method passed as an event handler three different ways
cases.question: The same store method is registered as a handler in three ways. Predict the four lines of output, and explain which registrations keep the store as the receiver.

criteria.description: Predicts handled: TypeError, handled: 1, handled: 2, items: y,z in that order.

Explains that passing store.add passes only the function, so handler(payload) runs with this undefined and the class body is strict; the arrow wrapper calls store.add(item) as a method call; bind fixes the receiver to store.

wrongModels.claim: A class method is bound to its instance automatically.
Wrapping the method in an arrow function also loses the receiver.
